findings.description: storage_encrypted is explicitly set to false, meaning the RDS instance's underlying storage, snapshots, and backups are not encrypted, exposing data at rest if the storage is compromised.
publicly_accessible is set to true, exposing the MySQL database instance directly to the internet rather than restricting it to the private network layer.
The database master username is hardcoded to the well-known default 'admin', making credential guessing/brute-force attacks easier against a publicly accessible instance.

The database password (var.password) is written in plaintext into the EC2 instance's user_data script and subsequently into a world-readable-by-describe-permission dbinfo.inc file, exposing the credential to anyone with EC2 describe permissions.

The inline policy grants wildcard actions (s3:*, ec2:*, rds:*) on all resources (Resource: *), giving the EC2 instance role far more privilege than needed to serve a web application, violating least privilege and enabling broad lateral movement if the instance is compromised.
The security group rule allows all outbound traffic (protocol -1, ports 0-0) to 0.0.0.0/0, providing an unrestricted data exfiltration and command-and-control channel from the RDS security group.
